context.title: Choose This Day
context.summary: At Shechem, Joshua retells Israel's story from Abraham to the conquest and calls the people to choose whom they will serve. They pledge to serve the Lord and renew the covenant. Joshua dies at 110, and Joseph's bones are buried at Shechem.
context.background: Shechem was where Abraham first built an altar in Canaan (Genesis 12:6-7) and where Jacob bought land (Genesis 33:19). Israel's ancestors had served other gods 'on the other side of the flood' (v. 2), meaning beyond the Euphrates River. Burying Joseph's bones fulfilled his dying request (Genesis 50:25).

customs.note: Joshua set up a large stone under the oak at the sanctuary, as if it had 'heard' the covenant and could testify to it.

watchFor: God speaks in the first person: 'I took... I gave... I brought' (vv. 3–13).
'As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord' (v. 15).
Joshua's startling reply, 'Ye cannot serve the Lord' (v. 19).

w: and he will make an end of

people.name: Joshua
people.summary: Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel.

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

people.name: Terah
people.summary: The wanderer; loiterer, for some unknown reason emigrated with his family from his native mountains in the north to the plains of Mesopotamia.

people.name: Nahor
people.summary: The father of Terah, who was the father of Abraham (Gen. 11:22-25; Luke 3:34).

people.name: Isaac
people.summary: The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3).

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

people.name: Balaam
people.summary: Lord of the people; foreigner or glutton, as interpreted by others, the son of Beor, was a man of some rank among the Midianites (Num. 31:8; comp. 16).

people.name: Balak
people.summary: Empty; spoiler, a son of Zippor, and king of the Moabites (Num. 22:2, 4).

people.name: Beor
people.summary: The father of Balaam (Num. 22:5; 24:3, 15; 31:8).

people.name: Zippor
people.summary: A little bird, the father of Balak, king of Moab (Num. 22:2, 4).

people.name: Nun
people.summary: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him (Ex. 33:11).

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.”

people.name: Shechem
people.summary: The son of Hamor the Hivite (Gen. 33:19; 34).

people.name: Hamor
people.summary: He-ass, a Hivite from whom Jacob purchased the plot of ground in which Joseph was afterwards buried (Gen. 33:19). He is called “Emmor” in Acts 7:16.

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32).

people.name: Phinehas
people.summary: Son of Eleazar, the high priest (Ex. 6:25). While yet a youth he distinguished himself at Shittim by his zeal against the immorality into which the Moabites had tempted the people (Num. 25:1-9), and thus “stayed the plague” that had broken out among the people, and by which twenty-four thousand of them perished.

places.name: Shechem
places.summary: A city in Samaria (Gen. 33:18), called also Sichem (12:6), Sychem (Acts 7:16). It stood in the narrow sheltered valley between Ebal on the north and Gerizim on the south, these mountains at their base being only some 500 yards apart.

places.name: Canaan
places.summary: The country which derived its name from the preceding. The name as first used by the Phoenicians denoted only the maritime plain on which Sidon was built.

places.name: river
places.summary: An event recorded in Gen. 7 and 8. In Josh. 24:2, 3, 14, 15, the word “flood” (R.V., “river”) means the river Euphrates.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Seir
places.summary: The name of a mountainous region occupied by the Edomites, extending along the eastern side of the Arabah from the south-eastern extremity of the Dead Sea to near the Akabah, or the eastern branch of the Red Sea.

places.name: Red sea
places.summary: The sea so called extends along the west coast of Arabia for about 1,400 miles, and separates Asia from Africa. It is connected with the Indian Ocean, of which it is an arm, by the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb.

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Josh. 3:16).

places.name: Gaash
places.summary: A shaking, a hill, on the north side of which Joshua was buried (Josh. 24:30; Judg. 2:9), in the territory of Ephraim.

places.name: Timnath-serah
places.summary: Remaining portion, the city of Joshua in the hill country of Ephraim, the same as Timnath-heres (Josh. 19:50; 24:30). “Of all sites I have seen,” says Lieut.

events.title: Death of Joshua
events.summary: Passage: Joshua 24:29 – Judges 2:8. People: Joshua. Place: Timnath-serah.
